ground_truth_witness:
Structural fact the script makes mechanical: every element of gamma_1 = beta_1 x beta_2 is a block-respecting direct product pi_1 x pi_2, hence lies in the SUBGROUP Sym(V_1) x Sym(V_2) of Sym(V_1 u V_2). Since that is a group, <S_1> is contained in Sym(V_1) x Sym(V_2) for EVERY choice S_1 subset-of alpha_1 subset-of gamma_1. So any block-mixing automorphism of M_{(1,2)} is a finite witness against "<S_1> = Aut(M_{(1,2)})".

MINIMAL HUMAN-CHECKABLE WITNESS (Search A, n = 3, blocks non-isomorphic, everything connected): M_{(1,2)} = path with edges {0,1},{0,2}; V_1 = V(H_1) = {0,1} (H_1 = K_2), V_2 = V(H_2) = {2} (H_2 = K_1). Aut(M) = {id, tau} with tau = (0->0, 1->2, 2->1), order 2 (verified exactly: tau maps the edge set onto itself). tau(V_1) = {0,2} != {0,1} = V_1, so tau is block-mixing and can never be written as pi_1 x pi_2. gamma_1^max = Aut(H_1) x Aut(H_2) has order 2*1 = 2, but gamma_1 ∩ Aut(M) = {id}, so the largest possible <S_1> has order 1. Claim says |<S_1>| = |Aut(M_{(1,2)})| = 2; here |<S_1>| = 1 < 2.

LARGEST-GAP NON-DEGENERATE WITNESS (Search A, n = 6, both blocks of size >= 2, admissible generating set already nontrivial): M_{(1,2)} = K_6, V_1 = {0,1,2} (H_1 = K_3), V_2 = {3,4,5} (H_2 = K_3). |Aut(M)| = 720; gamma_1^max = Aut(H_1) x Aut(H_2) has order 6*6 = 36 and all 36 of its elements ARE automorphisms of M, so the best possible S_1 generates a group of order exactly 36. Explicit block-mixing witness tau = (0->0,1->1,2->3,3->2,4->4,5->5) in Aut(M) with tau(V_1) = {0,1,3} != V_1. Claim says |<S_1>| = |Aut(M_{(1,2)})| = 720; here |<S_1>| = 36 < 720 (index 20). There are 684 block-mixing automorphisms in this single instance.

NON-ISOMORPHIC LARGE WITNESS (n = 6): M = K_6, V_1 = {0,1} (H_1 = K_2), V_2 = {2,3,4,5} (H_2 = K_4): |Aut(M)| = 720, largest possible |<S_1>| = |Aut(K_2)|*|Aut(K_4)| = 2*24 = 48 < 720; witness tau = (0->0,1->2,2->1,3->3,4->4,5->5).

WITNESS FOR THE VERBATIM SENTENCE, WITH AMBIENT H (Search B, n = 3): H = path with edges {0,1},{0,2}; V(H_1) = {1}, V(H_2) = {2}, so V(H_1) u V(H_2) = {1,2} is a proper subset of V(H). pi_a = (0->0, 1->2, 2->1) is in Aut(H) (edge set preserved, checked exactly) and satisfies pi_a(V(H_1) u V(H_2)) = {1,2}, i.e. it "acts on the vertices of H_1 u H_2". But pi_a(V_1) = {2} != {1} = V_1, so pi_a restricted to M_{(1,2)} mixes the blocks and therefore cannot lie in <S_1>, contradicting "pi_a in <S_1> = Aut(M_{(1,2)})".

The script asserts, for every reported witness, that (a) tau really is an automorphism (edge-set equality, exact), (b) the block-respecting automorphisms already form a closed subgroup (its generated closure has the same order), so the counting comparison is not an artifact of taking too small a generating set.
ground_truth_flaw: The proof's key soundness claim (Step 2 / Case 2): the set alpha_1, built only from block-respecting direct products in gamma_1 = beta_1 x beta_2, yields a generating set S_1 with <S_1> = Aut(M_{(1,2)}), so any automorphism of H acting on the vertices of H_1 union H_2 lies in <S_1>. This fails because Aut(M_{(1,2)}) can contain block-mixing automorphisms that are not direct products pi_1 x pi_2 and hence can never appear in gamma_1, alpha_1, or the group they generate.
